ai.title: Add lockfiles to default ignored files
ai.summary: Added `package-lock.json` and `bun.lockb` to `DEFAULT_IGNORED_FILES` in `common/src/constants.ts`. Prevents agent from processing large dependency manifests. Scope limited to core shared constants.

eli5.text: If you store a list of files that the assistant normally leaves alone, it now skips two big dependency-list files that can be very large and slow things down. This only affects the default list of ignored files and is live now.

ai.title: Suppress redundant output when prompt detected in tool handler
ai.summary: Removes manual stdout writing and newline appending when a prompt is detected in `handleRunTerminalCommand` within `npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts`. This prevents duplicate output display, as the stream is already handled elsewhere or disposed immediately after detection. Scope is limited to the terminal command tool handler. The `dataDisposable` and `clearTimeout` calls remain to properly clean up the listener.

eli5.text: When the terminal tool sees a prompt on the screen it now stops printing the repeated text immediately, instead of adding an extra blank line and duplicating what was just shown. You would notice that the output appears once and stays clean, without a second copy of the prompt text and an extra newline. This only affects the terminal command tool inside the app, and the cleanup of the listening code still happens the same way.

ai.title: Add average spend calculation script
ai.summary: New `scripts/calculate-average-spend.ts` computes average monthly spend per customer from Stripe invoices. It aggregates paid invoices from the last 30 days, normalizes cents to dollars, and outputs total spend, average per customer, and spend distribution buckets. Internal tooling only; no user-facing behavior changes.

eli5.text: A new internal tool now calculates how much the company makes on average from each paying customer each month. The tool pulls every payment received through Stripe during the past 30 days, converts that amount from cents to dollars, totals it up, divides by the number of customers, and then prints out not just the average but how many customers fall into different spending ranges. Since this is an internal-only script that runs manually, you won’t notice any change when using the product. If you’re an employee with access to the system, you’d see this new script in the scripts folder that can be run to instantly report the latest customer spending numbers.

ai.title: Extract runTerminalCommand to utils/terminal
ai.summary: Moved `runTerminalCommand`, `resetPtyShell`, and PTY logic from `npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts` to new file `npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts`. Added `truncateStringWithMessage` helper in `common/src/util/string.ts` to handle output truncation with explicit markers. Updated imports in `npm-app/src/index.ts` and `tool-handlers.ts` to reflect the new module structure. This refactor isolates terminal execution concerns from general tool handlers.

eli5.text: The assistant now runs terminal commands through a single dedicated module instead of scattering that logic inside the general tool-handling code, so long command output that could overwhelm the view gets cleanly cut off with a clear marker telling you it was shortened. If you watched the system work today, you'd see terminal-related behavior behaving the same from the outside, but internally the command-running and shell-setup code lives together in one tidy place, making it easier to keep working correctly. This is behind-the-scenes cleanup that doesn't change what you can do, just how reliably and clearly the assistant handles terminal tasks.

ai.title: Code search output preview limited to 3 lines
ai.summary: handleCodeSearch in npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts now prints up to 3 lines of raw grep results before the count. Header format changed to 'Searching [basename] for "pattern":'. Full output remains truncated to 10000 chars for the agent.

eli5.text: When you ask the coding assistant to search your project's files for a specific term or phrase, you'll now see up to three actual example matches printed out right away, followed by a total count of how many matches were found overall. The search summary line now shows the project's folder name and wraps your search term in quotes, like: Searching my-project for "blue-button":. If you see "..." after the examples, it just means there were more matches than the three shown. This is live today, no settings to turn on.

ai.title: Fix stream start event for empty chunks in client
ai.summary: The client now checks `chunk.trim()` before triggering `onStreamStart()`. This prevents the stream start event from firing on empty or whitespace-only chunks, ensuring it only activates when actual content is received. The change affects `npm-app/src/client.ts`.

eli5.text: The assistant now waits to receive actual text before announcing that a reply has started, instead of announcing it the moment the connection opens. You would notice this if you sometimes saw the assistant appear to start answering before any words appeared, which will no longer happen. This only affects the chat client used by the internal tooling, so nothing changes for end users of the main product.

ai.title: Terminal shell config sourcing and Windows prompt simplification
ai.summary: Terminal initialization now sources shell RC files (~/.zshrc, config.fish, ~/.bashrc, PowerShell profile) to match real terminal behavior. Windows environment variables were adjusted to set PROMPT='$P$G' for reliable parsing, and prompt detection regexes were consolidated to remove redundant patterns. Changes affect npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts and npm-app/knowledge.md.

eli5.text: The assistant now starts up its terminal session by loading your shell's startup files (like ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc) and sets a few environment variables, so it behaves more like a real terminal you'd open yourself. On Windows, it configures a simpler prompt (PROMPT='$P$G') and consolidates prompt-detection patterns to reduce redundant or confusing output. You wouldn't notice a dramatic difference day-to-day, but the terminal should feel more consistent and produce fewer duplicate or garbled lines, especially when running commands that interact with your shell configuration.

ai.title: Terminal PTY spawn adds login flag, UTF-8 locale, resize handler
ai.summary: createPty in npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts spawns Unix shells with `--login` flag and sets `LANG`/`LC_ALL` to `en_US.UTF-8`. Windows PTY spawn remains flagless. Added `process.stdout.on('resize')` handler forwards `pty.resize` to persistent process. `SHELL` env var now strips `.exe` suffix via `shell.split('.')[0]`. Documented in npm-app/knowledge.md.

eli5.text: When you open a terminal window inside the app on a Mac or Linux machine, the program now starts it up exactly the way your regular terminal would, loading all your personal settings like aliases, history, and environment variables such as display language (set to U.S. English with UTF-8 support), so commands and text appear consistently formatted. The terminal also adjusts its size automatically if you resize the window or change screen resolution, keeping the layout correct, though this only applies to Mac and Linux and not Windows where the terminal starts up without these extra startup arguments but still respects your preferred editor settings.

ai.title: Terminal execution timeout raised to 30 seconds
ai.summary: MAX_EXECUTION_TIME constant in npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts increased from 10_000 to 30_000 milliseconds. Allows longer-running commands to complete without premature termination. Internal utility change affecting terminal command execution limits.

eli5.text: Commands that the assistant runs in your terminal now get up to 30 seconds to finish instead of the previous 10-second cut-off. If you triggered a command that took, say, 20 seconds to complete, it previously would have been killed and reported as failed; today it can finish and return its full output. This is a behind-the-scenes tweak to an internal timing limit, so you probably won't notice anything unless you were hitting that old 10-second cliff.

ai.title: Remove --login flag from persistent PTY spawn
ai.summary: The `pty.spawn` call in `npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts` no longer passes `--login` to non-Windows shells. This change ensures persistent PTYs start without login shell overhead or potential profile conflicts. Scope is limited to the internal terminal utility used by the CLI.

eli5.text: When the assistant opens a new terminal window for you, it no longer starts the shell as a "login shell", which previously could slow things down or cause profile-loading conflicts. This only affects internal terminal handling used by the CLI, and is live today; nothing you did needs to change. You would notice slightly faster and smoother terminal startup without login-shell overhead.

ai.title: Upgrade @homebridge/node-pty-prebuilt-multiarch to 0.12.0-beta.5
ai.summary: Bumped optional dependency @homebridge/node-pty-prebuilt-multiarch from 0.11.14 to 0.12.0-beta.5 in npm-app/package.json. Update targets pty prebuilt multiarch support. Scope limited to npm-app package and lockfile.

eli5.text: The system quietly swapped out one piece of background technology that lets the app run external terminal programs, leaving the rest of the software untouched. This only affects how the app manages those external helper programs behind the scenes, so nothing you see or do in the app changes. The swap is already in place in the developer files and will take effect the next time the app is built or updated.

ai.title: Bump codebuff npm package to 1.0.138
ai.summary: Version bump in `npm-app/package.json` from 1.0.137 to 1.0.138. Internal release for the `codebuff` package. No functional changes or user-facing features added.

eli5.text: The assistant's package manager now automatically ignores lockfiles so they don't clutter searches or get accidentally edited, and the terminal command runner suppresses noisy duplicate prompts when a prompt is already detected. Behind the scenes, terminal handling was reorganized into its own module, the empty-chunk stream bug in the client was fixed, and code search previews are capped at three lines. An average-spend calculation script was also added. These changes ship live today.

ai.title: Fix terminal.ts import path
ai.summary: Corrected import path in `npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts` from `src/project-files` to `../project-files`. Resolves module resolution errors during build. No user-facing behavior change.

eli5.text: The assistant's tool that reads your project's files was pointing to the wrong location, so the program couldn't find what it needed while building. It now looks in the correct nearby folder instead, letting the build succeed without changing anything you see or do.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.139
ai.summary: Version bumped from 1.0.138 to 1.0.139. Change isolated to `npm-app/package.json`. No functional or structural code modifications.

eli5.text: The assistant's internal version number was ticked up to keep automatic updates flowing; there's nothing new you can see or click because of it. The only things actually changed since the last number are small behind-the-scenes fixes, like correcting a misplaced import path and a few tweaks that stop the tool from repeating itself or showing too many lines of search results. If you opened the project today you'd still find the same features and screens you used before, just running on this slightly newer build.
